newsitem.title: UK: Why girls are better babies than boys.
newsitem.headline: Why girls are better babies than boys.

text.p: Girls are better-behaved babies than boys because their mothers expect them to be, a British psychologist said on Friday.

Girls are more securely attached to their mothers at the age of 14 months than boys are, and it may be because the mother treats boys differently, Liz Connors of the University of Central Lancashire said.
She studied 31 boys and 24 girls as they interacted with their mothers from the age of 3-1/2 months to 14 months old.
"There was evidence of greater maternal sensitivity towards female infants, whereas males experienced more restrictions," she said. There were few differences in male and female behaviour.
"However, males were found to be fussier than females at three and a half months," she said. "There was also some indication that male infants may be perceived as more difficult than females."
The babies responded in very different ways to their mothers. Boys became fussy when their mothers were "intrusive," trying to interfere with the way they moved or played.
Girls, on the other hand, became difficult when their mothers were more affectionate.

Therefore, Connors said, it appeared that mothers reacted differently to boy and girl babies. "The findings may also explain why boys may be more predisposed to developing behaviour problems than girls," she told a meeting of the British Psychological Society.
